title: Warehouse throughput collapse
case_study: A regional distribution centre saw order throughput fall 34% over six weeks. Headcount was unchanged and inbound volume was flat. The floor supervisor attributes it to a new pick-path algorithm rolled out in week one; the vendor attributes it to seasonal SKU mix. No A/B window was held before the rollout and the prior algorithm was decommissioned.

title: Duplicate refunds after migration
case_study: Following a payments-platform migration, 1,180 customers received a refund twice within 48 hours. The reconciliation job ran against the legacy ledger for two days after cutover because its cron entry was never repointed. Finance caught it on the daily variance report. No customer complained; every duplicate was outbound.

title: Clinic no-show rate spike
case_study: An outpatient clinic's no-show rate rose from 8% to 21% after switching its reminder vendor. The new vendor sends SMS at 09:00 two days ahead; the old one sent at 18:00 the evening before. The clinic also moved to online-only booking in the same month, and the patient mix shifted toward a younger cohort.

title: Contractor invoice mismatch
case_study: A facilities contractor invoiced for 2,400 hours in a month where badge data shows 1,650 hours on site. The contract permits off-site preparation time, which is not badge-tracked and has never been itemised. The contractor has provided timesheets signed by a manager who left the organisation in the period under review.

title: Model drift in fraud screening
case_study: A fraud-screening model's precision fell from 0.91 to 0.68 over one quarter while recall held steady. No code or threshold change was deployed. A new merchant category was onboarded in the same quarter, contributing 12% of volume, and the training set has not been refreshed in fourteen months.

title: Grant acquittal shortfall
case_study: A community organisation acquitted a 400,000 grant with 380,000 of documented spend. The 20,000 gap is attributed to in-kind volunteer labour valued at an internal rate never agreed with the funder. The grant deed permits in-kind contribution but is silent on valuation method. The acquittal deadline is in eleven days.

title: Rolling outage after failover test
case_study: A scheduled failover test triggered a four-hour partial outage. Failover itself succeeded in 90 seconds; the outage came from failback, where stale connection pools in three downstream services held references to the retired primary. The runbook covers failover and does not mention failback. The test had passed in staging, which runs a single service.

title: Procurement single-source justification
case_study: A 1.2M software renewal was approved as single-source on the ground that migration cost exceeded the price delta. The migration estimate was supplied by the incumbent vendor and not independently reviewed. Two competitors were not approached. The approving delegate holds authority to 1.5M and the renewal is nineteen days from lapse.
